sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup and PDF library
sections.what: Describes the module and loads WeasyPrint, the type helpers and the logger.
sections.why: The module description says this file creates PDF reports from results.
sections.watch_out: If WeasyPrint or its system libraries are missing, this import fails, and the app may fail to start.

sections.name: generate_html_report (part 1)
sections.title: Building the report page styles and header
sections.what: Creates the HTML text for the report: style rules for headings, tables and highlights, a title with the model name, and summary lines for model, scenario and currency.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the page layout and styling in one template.
sections.watch_out: Model and scenario names go straight into the markup, so unusual characters can break the page.

sections.name: generate_html_report (part 2)
sections.title: Report section placeholders
sections.what: Adds the four headings (income statement, cash flow, balance sheet and DCF valuation), each with an empty placeholder. The results data is not used yet.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The placeholders mark where the tables will go later.
sections.watch_out: The report looks finished to a reader but has no numbers, so it could be mistaken for a complete report.

sections.name: export_to_pdf
sections.title: Writing the PDF file
sections.what: Builds the HTML, logs the start, writes the PDF to the given file name with WeasyPrint, logs completion and returns the file name.
sections.why: Likely reason: one call hides the two steps (HTML first, then PDF) from callers.
sections.watch_out: If the location is not writable or WeasyPrint fails, the error is passed on to the caller with no friendly message.

summary: Turns model results into a PDF report with WeasyPrint. The report currently has a title block and empty headings for each statement, with no figures yet.
purpose: Lets the user download a printable report of the model.
why: Likely reason: writing HTML and converting it to PDF is a common way to make styled reports. The reason is not otherwise stated in the code.
how: 1. Builds an HTML page with styling, a title, the model name, the scenario name and the currency. 2. Adds headings for income statement, cash flow, balance sheet and DCF valuation, each with a placeholder. 3. Passes the HTML to WeasyPrint, which writes the PDF file.
inputs: model_data with name and currency. scenario_data with name. results, which is accepted but not used yet. The output file name.
outputs: A PDF file at the given name. The function returns that name.
risks: The report has no numbers yet. Model and scenario names are placed into the HTML without escaping, so unusual characters can break the layout. WeasyPrint needs system libraries installed, and it may fail on some computers.
debug: If the PDF fails to create, check that WeasyPrint and its system libraries are installed. If the PDF has headings but no figures, that is expected because the tables are placeholders. A KeyError means model_data or scenario_data is missing a field.
